title: Create Mixture Design
selectedvars: Select mixture components (2+ numeric columns from the active dataset)
lblComponentNote: The active dataset should have exactly 2 rows for the selected component columns: row 1 = lower bound, row 2 = upper bound for each component, expressed in the SAME units as 'Total amount' below (e.g., 0 to 100 if Total = 100). For an unconstrained mixture (Simplex Lattice or Simplex Centroid), leave row 1 = 0 and row 2 = Total for every component.
totalAmount: Total amount (components should sum to this value)
latticeDegree: Degree (m) — model order this design supports (1=linear, 2=quadratic, 3=special cubic, ...)
verticesChk: Extreme Vertices Design (uses the component bounds above)
addCentroidChk: Add the overall/constrained centroid point if not already included
numOfReplicates: Number of replicates (repeats the full point set)
lbl1: You may not need to change the randomization settings

help.title: Create Mixture Design
help.r_help: No external package required — all generation logic is implemented directly.
help.body:
Description
Creates a mixture design — an experiment where two or more components are proportions of a whole that must sum to a fixed total (typically 100%). Unlike a factorial design, mixture components cannot be varied independently: increasing one component's proportion requires decreasing one or more of the others.

How designs are generated (no external R package required)
  • Simplex Lattice: generated directly via an exact stars-and-bars integer composition enumeration (produces exactly N = C(q+m−1, m) points, no wasted computation even for larger component counts or degrees).
  • Simplex Centroid: generated directly by taking the centroid of every non-empty subset of components (2^q − 1 points).
  • Extreme Vertices: generated directly by fixing q−1 components at a lower or upper bound and solving for the remaining component via the sum constraint, keeping only feasible results and removing duplicates. This is the standard method for regions defined purely by individual component bounds (not more general linear constraints between components).
Preparing your data
Before opening this dialog, create a small table with one column per mixture component and exactly two rows:
  • Row 1 = the lower bound for each component
  • Row 2 = the upper bound for each component
Bounds should be expressed in the same units as "Total amount" (e.g., if Total = 100, enter bounds as percentages such as 10 and 40, not 0.10 and 0.40). For an unconstrained design (Simplex Lattice or Simplex Centroid), simply set every lower bound to 0 and every upper bound to the Total amount — bounds are only actually used by the Extreme Vertices design type.

Design Types — which to choose
  • Simplex Lattice: "Tell me how finely to divide the mixture space." Best when the mixture region is the full simplex and you want a regular, degree-controlled design.
  • Simplex Centroid: "Test every possible subset of ingredients at equal proportions." A highly symmetric design with no degree parameter. Grows as 2^q − 1, so it becomes impractical for many components (255 runs at 8 components) — this dialog will warn you when that is likely to be a concern.
  • Extreme Vertices: "Tell me the actual allowable range for every ingredient, and design experiments only inside that feasible region." Use this whenever any component cannot range freely between 0 and the Total.
Model order supported by Degree (m)
  • m = 1: linear Scheffé model (main effects only)
  • m = 2: quadratic Scheffé model (adds all pairwise component interactions) — the most commonly used order
  • m = 3: special cubic model
  • higher m: increasingly complex mixture surfaces
Analyzing the design
Use the companion "Analyze Mixture Design" dialog, or fit a mixture (Scheffé-type, no-intercept) model directly with lm() — for example: Y ~ -1 + (Comp1 + Comp2 + Comp3)^2.

Not currently supported in this dialog
Interior/edge point augmentation beyond the base design points and the overall/constrained centroid (previously available via an external package's Fillv-style function). For designs needing additional interior points at an exact run count, use Create D-Optimal Mixture Design instead.
